name: Spectrum Violet
lede: Spectrum Violet is a deep, saturated violet from Ridgway's 1912 atlas; the books do not explain the name, but they do explain why violet is not purple.

sections.title: Violet is not purple
sections.body:
Eckstut and Siegel stress that the color we see at the end of a rainbow is violet, not purple, and that purple would be the wrong word for the spectrum's last band [1]. In color science the two are separate categories, though in everyday English the words are often swapped [1].

The color name itself comes from Ridgway's *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* of 1912, where it sits on plate X, hue 59 [2]. Our swatch is taken from a scan of an aged plate, so it is approximate [2]. The ISCC-NBS system files it under "strong violet", 3.0 CIEDE2000 units away [2].

The books add a fact about how we see the end of the spectrum. The short-wavelength cones, needed for blue and violet, also feed into how red looks, and the long-wavelength cones have a small second sensitivity peak in the blue-violet range [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This is a color painters rarely used at this saturation. No painting in our archive of 23,781 has it covering at least 1 per cent of the canvas, within a CIEDE2000 distance of 4, as photographed [3]. That describes the archive, not painting as a whole, and varnish and age mute violets in photographs [3].
